[T3 Code: the agent in T3 thread "9b581f9e-99f2-4346-8611-1ad1fdba6dd5" sent this message, not the user.]

Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

You are implementing PR 6 (the last) of a stacked series in Moneo. Follow AGENTS.md exactly (no comments, test rules, QA backend only — never the owner's backend or port 3000; migrations per "Database changes", must work in the desktop bundle without pg_cron etc.; new data folders/storage must be covered by desktop backup/restore; Speed section; screenshots embedded in the PR).

Stacking: `git fetch origin`, create branch `t3/settings-6-logs` from `origin/t3/settings-5-diagnostics` (PR #345 → #344 → #343 → #342 → #341). Open your PR with base `t3/settings-5-diagnostics`. PR 5 built `/settings/diagnostics` (reachable only from Settings) with section chips (Usage, Health) and an `ai_usage` ledger written through one helper that every model must use. Add a "Logs" section/chip there.

Owner's requirement (their words, condensed): Moneo is open source; when someone has a problem they should see the logs directly and troubleshoot or share them with us. Store logs of EVERYTHING that happens while using the app:
- server errors and warnings (the ~30 `console.error`/`console.warn` sites in app/, lib/, workflows/ should go through one logger that both prints and stores), client errors in the browser (error boundaries, unhandled rejections, failed fetches) sent to a local endpoint, background jobs/workflows (start, stage, finish, error), bank and Scalable syncs, imports, scheduler/cron runs,
- every AI interaction: chat requests and replies INCLUDING the model's thinking/reasoning, tool calls and results, agent runs, organizer decisions, artifacts — link to the `ai_usage` row,
- voice: voice-call audio (both sides if available), text-to-speech output audio, and speech-to-text input audio (the audio file itself) with the transcript.
Audio goes to the existing Storage service (bucket, RLS per workspace), text/events to a log table (new migration, `lib/schema.ts`, `npm run db:types` on the test backend). Logging must never block or slow the user's action (fire-and-forget with a named failure handler per lint rules) — measure chat time-to-first-token and a page open before/after.

Retention: a setting on the Logs section (and saved like other settings via the workspace settings Zod schema — a stored value this version can't read must never block sign-in): 1 week, 14 days (DEFAULT), 30 days, 90 days, Forever. A daily job (`lib/scheduler.ts` / `cronRoute()`, or the existing daily maintenance if any) deletes text logs and audio older than the setting — test the cutoff math with the owner's time zone. "Reset all data" clears logs and audio. Logs are NOT readable by the AI chat (no read scope).

Logs UI on Diagnostics: newest first, filter by level (error/warn/info), area (AI, voice, sync, import, jobs, app/server, browser) and time; search text; expand an entry to see details (JSON), its linked conversation/run/usage row, and an audio player for audio entries; paging/virtualization so thousands of entries stay fast. "Copy for a bug report" (and "Download" as a .txt/.json file) for the current filtered selection, with REDACTION: money amounts, IBANs/account numbers, names of people/merchants/accounts, emails, API keys/tokens/secrets, and audio excluded — show a preview of exactly what will be copied. Put redaction in a pure `lib/` function with thorough tests (that's real behaviour: leaked IBAN/key = bug). Also a "Delete all logs now" action with confirmation.

Hit every surface: FEATURES.md (`npm run feature-map`), README (what is logged, where it's stored, retention, how to share for a bug report — note it stays on the owner's machine), `.env.example` only if a new variable is needed (avoid), desktop backup/restore if storage layout changes, privacy (`npm run check:privacy`). Mobile, light and dark.

Workflow: commit in steps, messages end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Mock AI/bank/Scalable in tests; seed logs (including a short synthetic TTS-like audio clip, no real voice) on QA for screenshots and remove after. Before/after screenshots (skill `verify-ui`) light/dark/mobile: Diagnostics before, Logs list, an expanded AI entry with thinking, an audio entry with player, the redaction preview, the retention setting. Run `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run check:bundle`, `npm run test:db`, affected Playwright. Push, open PR titled "Diagnostics: logs of everything with audio and a retention setting", screenshots uploaded so they render (as earlier PRs did on the `pr-assets` branch), Speed and Decisions sections, body ends with "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)". If something can't be captured (e.g. browser-only voice audio), open a GitHub issue and list it. Do not merge. Final line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

1. **Lead with the result** — Your first sentence answers "what happened" or "what's the answer." No preamble ("Let me...", "Now I'll...") and no closing recap of what you already said.
2. **Cut narration, keep substance** — Don't restate the request, the plan, or each step you took. Report outcomes, decisions, and anything the user must act on.
3. **Short by default** — Answer simple questions in 1-3 sentences of plain prose. Use headers, tables, and bullet lists only when they carry real structure, never as decoration.

6. **Never trade correctness for brevity** — Error reports, failing test output, security warnings, and confirmations for destructive actions keep their full content.

Where these rules conflict with more general communication or formatting guidance elsewhere in your instructions, these rules win.

Use when the owner corrects a mistake, says "stop doing X", "always do Y" or "make this a rule", when the same fix is needed a second time, or when the tempting fix is another sentence in AGENTS.md or in the assistant's system prompt.
- state-chart: Draw the state machine of a Moneo flow as a diagram the owner can review, taken from the code, and list the paths that break a rule. Use when a change adds or alters a multi-step flow (import, bank connect and reconnect, Scalable orders, proposal cards, voice call, agent runs, desktop start-up), when asked to "draw the states", "show the flow" or "state chart", or to show a bug as a path through states.
- verify-ui: Prove a Moneo change works by driving the real QA app the way the owner would, and attach the evidence (screenshots in light, dark and mobile, or a recording) to the pull request. Use after any change to a page, component, style or user flow, when asked to "verify", "show me it works" or "add screenshots", and before opening a PR that changes what the owner sees.
- claude-security:attack-surface-analysis: Attack surface analysis: a long audit in three stages (default attack surface reduction, early reachability audit, configuration interaction audit) that ends in reports and patch files, with every finding challenged by an independent agent. Use only when the user asks for such an analysis or audit: an attack surface analysis or reduction, an audit of what is reachable before login (pre-authentication) or 0-click, a protocol state machine audit, or a configuration interaction audit. Use it too when the user asks to apply a patch that such an analysis wrote. Do not use it to answer a question about the code, such as what an attacker can reach. It is not a vulnerability scan: to scan code or find vulnerabilities, use the claude-security:claude-security skill.
- claude-security:claude-security: Claude Security: scan the codebase (the whole repository or a scoped part of it), scan changes (this branch's or a pull request's diff, or one commit), triage existing findings (another scanner's SARIF file or an earlier report, checked against the code), or suggest patches (findings turned into targeted patch files, each analyzed by a panel of agents, that you apply when you choose). Use when the user asks to scan, audit or check code with Claude Security, to scan their changes with Claude Security, to triage, validate or prioritize a SARIF file's or an earlier report's findings with the Claude Security plugin, or to fix or patch the findings of a report that this plugin wrote.
- claude-security:hosted: Hosted Claude Security: list what it has open for this repository, show one of its findings from a link or an ID (also to fix it), check on a project, or say how to add this repository. Load it before reading from a Claude Security connector or MCP tool: when the user asks about hosted Claude Security projects or findings, or pastes a claude.ai/security link, a find_... ID, or a prompt copied from Claude Security. Not for resolving or reopening a finding, nor for a project's documents.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- ship-local (ship): Commit and push your work and open a pull request if the branch has none, review it in this session, fix the real problems, then watch the pull request (CI failures, conflicts, and review comments) until it is merged or closed. Claude is told never to merge the pull request. - Never call it yourself: only a line that the user types starts it. If they ask for it in other words, tell them to type /ship.
- steward: Watch the current branch's open pull request in this session and handle CI failures, conflicts, and review comments until it's merged or closed. It doesn't review the code first. Claude is told never to merge the pull request. - Never call it yourself: only a line that the user types starts it. If they ask for it in other words, tell them to type /steward.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read FIRST, before you answer, run a command or open a file (already started? read it now); don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- plugin-authoring: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a theme, a panel or pane that stays beside the chat and updates, a band, status line, toast, slash command, or hook on tool calls. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:chrome-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:computer-use: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.

If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. - anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.

Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy, rename, move or trash a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.
- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.

This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:setup-writing-style: Learns how the user writes from their own sent messages and docs, and builds a voice profile so future drafts sound like them instead of generic AI. The profile is saved as the my-writing-style skill. Use when the user asks to set up, learn, or capture their writing voice, or complains that drafts sound generic or unlike them and no my-writing-style profile exists. Only for drafting text the user will send as themselves, not for Claude's own replies.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. # AGENTS.md

Moneo is an open-source personal-finance app you run on your own computer. One owner imports statements or syncs a bank, tracks accounts and wealth, plans spending, and asks about their money in chat, artifacts and voice calls.

Moneo ships two ways from this one codebase: the desktop app (`desktop/`, Electron, what most owners install) and the source installation (`npm run setup` + Docker). Every change must work in both.

Stack: Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript. The backend is Postgres plus the open-source Supabase Auth, PostgREST and Storage services: in Docker for the source installation (`docker-compose.yml`), as bundled native processes in the desktop app (`desktop/src/backend/`). Drizzle schema, Workflow (local world) for durable jobs, Vitest and Playwright, and the Vercel AI SDK, paid by the owner's ChatGPT plan or an API key.

These are defaults. The developer's instructions override them; if a rule conflicts with the task, say so and ask.

## Non-negotiables

- **Local-first.** Everything listens on `127.0.0.1`; optional phone access is Tailscale forwarding to it (`lib/phone-access.ts`). Data leaves the machine only for services the owner set up (AI provider, Enable Banking, Scalable). New features must work fully offline from the cloud except those calls.
- **One owner, no accounts.** The proxy signs the owner in automatically; there is no sign-up or sign-in screen. Private access from the owner's own Tailscale devices needs no login; anything public must add one first.
- **Financial truth comes from code and data, never from AI guesses.** Money is integer minor units (`bigint`) with an explicit currency. The AI explains and proposes; every write it suggests is a card the owner accepts.
- **Two AI writes skip cards.** The organizer applies high- and medium-confidence category and merchant labels itself, marked as AI (`organized_by = 'ai'`), listed with every other AI decision and undoable; they never become owner rules or owner corrections. The chat tool `transactions_setCategory` sets the category the owner named for the exact transaction they named, audited and undoable. Every other AI write is a card.
- **History is kept.** Preserve source records, corrections, history and undo when changing financial data flows.
- **Open source.** No secrets, private statements or personal data in the repo (`npm run check:privacy` runs before tests and lint).

## How to work

1. **Think before coding.** State your assumptions. If a request has more than one reading, name them and ask instead of picking silently. If a simpler approach exists, say so.
2. **Simplicity first.** Write the least code that solves the problem: no speculative features, options or single-use abstractions. Prefer existing utilities and dependencies, and Zod for validating user and external input. Would a senior engineer call it overcomplicated? Then simplify.
3. **Surgical changes.** Touch only what the task needs and match the nearby style. Remove what your own change made unused; mention unrelated dead code instead of deleting it.
4. **Never write a comment.** Put the meaning in a name, a type, a test or a lint rule; if a comment would defend a workaround, fix the cause instead. `npm run lint` rejects comments (`moneo/no-comments` in `eslint.config.mjs`) except tool directives such as `eslint-disable-next-line <rule> -- reason`.
5. **Corrections become checks.** When a review correction could recur, enforce it with a lint rule, a type or a test whose error message says what to do instead. Add a line here only when it needs human judgment.
6. **Fix the class, not the case.** Trace a failure to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there, so every similar case is fixed with it. A guard, a retry, a swallowed error or a special case at the place it showed up hides the fault. When the assistant in the app cannot do something, give it the tool, data or scope it lacks; never add a sentence to its system prompt (`lib/ai/provider.ts`, `lib/ai/voice-*`) that names one request, keyword or example.
7. **Goal-driven.** Turn the task into checks you can run, then loop until they pass. A bug fix starts by reproducing the failure; see Tests for when that becomes a kept test. Purely visual changes get before/after screenshots instead (skill `verify-ui`).

## Safety

- Never run tests or experiments against the owner's backend (`.env`, Docker project `moneo`, app on port 3000). Tests use the separate test backend below, as its QA user or disposable users they create and remove.
- Never delete the `moneo` Docker volumes (`docker compose down -v`) or drop its database: that is the owner's financial history. The test backend is disposable: `docker compose -p moneo-qa down -v` then `npm run setup -- --qa` starts it fresh.
- Never change `JWT_SECRET`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` or `BANK_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in an existing `.env`; keys, sessions and stored bank and ChatGPT tokens stop working.
- Never commit `.env*` (except `.env.example`), `.data/`, `e2e/.auth.json` or `.qa/`.
- Only kill processes you started, or ones you verified by port and working directory. Never kill by name.
- Real AI, bank and Scalable calls cost money or count against limits (PSD2 allows about 4 background bank fetches a day). Mock them in tests unless the task is to check the real service.

## Hit every surface

Before calling a feature done, check where else it shows up:

- `FEATURES.md` (generated by `npm run feature-map`) lists every page, chat tool, voice route, widget, palette command, background job and undo path; find the feature's other entry points there.
- Pages and their mobile layout, light and dark.
- Chat tools and the system prompt in `lib/ai/provider.ts`, artifacts, and the voice call (`lib/ai/voice-*`).
- Home widgets and the command palette.
- Background jobs (`lib/scheduler.ts`, `workflows/`) and imports from files, banks and Scalable.
- The desktop app: see Desktop app below.
- The reverse path: undo, reset all data, reconnect, disconnect.
- Docs: `README.md` for anything the owner sets up or runs, the landing page in `docs/` when a headline feature or install step changes, `.env.example` for new variables. Deferred work goes in GitHub issues.

## Commands

Use npm (`package-lock.json` is authoritative).

- Install: `npm ci`
- Backend: `npm run setup` (writes `.env` secrets, starts Docker, applies migrations, creates the owner; safe to rerun)
- Dev: `npm run dev` (http://localhost:3000)
- Feature map: `npm run feature-map` regenerates `FEATURES.md`
- Unit: `npm test` · Lint: `npm run lint` · Build: `npm run build` · Bundle budget: `npm run check:bundle` (after a build)
- Database: `npm run test:db` (needs the backend from `npm run setup`) · `npm run db:types` regenerates `lib/database.types.ts` after a migration (needs the test backend)
- E2E: `npm run test:e2e` (see `e2e/README.md`)
- Desktop: `node scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs --platform <win-x64|mac-arm64|mac-x64|linux-x64>` once, then `npm run desktop:build`, `npm run desktop:dev`, `npm run desktop:dist` and `npm run desktop:smoke` (drives the packaged app)
- Desktop release: push a `v*` tag matching `desktop/package.json`, then publish the drafted release (`desktop/README.md` → Releasing). Never tag or publish unasked.

## Test backend

Everything that needs a database or a running app is tested against `moneo-qa`, never the owner's setup:

- **Backend:** Docker project `moneo-qa` (ports 54521/54522), secrets in the git-ignored `.env.qa` (one shared copy in `~/.moneo/qa.env`, so every worktree uses the same stack). Create, upgrade or copy it into a new worktree with `npm run setup -- --qa`; then `npm run qa:auth` creates the QA user and saves `e2e/.auth.json`.
- **App:** `npm run qa:server` runs this checkout on http://localhost:3100 against `.env.qa`, building into `.next-qa` (`QA_PORT=<port>` for another port), with bank access off and a placeholder AI key that every provider rejects, so nothing costs money. `npm run test:e2e` starts it on its own and refuses to run against any server that would sign tests in as the owner.
- **Screenshots:** `npm run qa:shots -- <label> home money/transactions` saves each page in light, dark and mobile to `.qa/shots/<label>/` and fails on a console error or a failed request (skill `verify-ui`).
- **Reset:** `npm run qa:reset` empties the QA workspace. Each spec should still set up the state it needs rather than rely on what earlier runs left behind.
- `npm run test:db` and the `supabase/tests/*.mjs` scripts read `.env.qa` only.
- A nightly run (`npm run qa:nightly`, see `e2e/README.md`) runs every spec twice and keeps the issue "Nightly browser suite is failing" up to date; fix what it lists before adding new specs.

## Desktop app

The Electron app (`desktop/README.md`, `desktop/src/backend/README.md`) runs the same Next.js server as a standalone build next to its own Postgres, GoTrue, PostgREST and Storage processes. There is no Docker, Node.js, terminal or `.env` on the owner's machine, so:

- **Settings the owner needs go in the app**, not in `.env`. `desktop:build` unsets every `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` and fails if a local address is baked in; desktop-only behaviour reads `MONEO_DESKTOP_*` at runtime.
- **Migrations run on the owner's existing database** at the next start, after an automatic `pre-upgrade` backup (`desktop/src/backend/migrations.ts`). They must work without the extensions the bundle lacks: supautils, pg_graphql, pg_net, pg_cron, pgsodium/vault, pg_stat_statements, realtime, and uuid-ossp on Windows.
- **The app lives on `http://localhost:47300`** (or the port saved in `shell.json`), not 3000. Get addresses from the request or from `appUrl()`, `loopbackUrl()` and `appPort()` in `lib/env.ts`; lint rejects a hard-coded 3000.
- **Sign-ins open in the system browser** and return through the loopback callbacks; the result reaches the window through `lib/desktop-bridge.ts` and `desktop/src/bridge.ts`. The window opens only Moneo's own pages and allows only the microphone and copying.
- **Files the server reads at runtime** by a dynamic path need `/*turbopackIgnore: true*/`, or the standalone build traces source files and `desktop:build` fails.
- **A new backend service, native module or data folder** must be added to `fetch-backend.mjs`, the start order, backup and restore, and the packaged files in `electron-builder.config.cjs`.
- **Keep the security fuses** (RunAsNode, `NODE_OPTIONS` and `--inspect` off; asar integrity on); `desktop:smoke` reads them back.
- Never test against the owner's installed app or its user-data folder; set `MONEO_DESKTOP_HOME` to a scratch folder.

The Desktop workflow builds and smoke-tests every platform on pull requests that touch `desktop/`, `scripts/desktop/`, `next.config.ts`, `package*.json` or `supabase/migrations/`.

## Project map

- `app/` — App Router pages, route handlers, server actions
- `components/` — shared UI
- `lib/finance/` — deterministic financial logic
- `lib/ai/` — models, chat tools, ChatGPT sign-in (`chatgpt.ts`), voice
- `lib/bank/`, `lib/scalable/` — Enable Banking and Scalable Capital
- `lib/schema.ts` + `supabase/migrations/` — database schema
- `workflows/` — durable background jobs; `lib/scheduler.ts` runs the daily ones
- `docker-compose.yml`, `docker/`, `scripts/setup.mjs` — the self-hosted backend
- `e2e/` — Playwright flows; `supabase/tests/` — SQL regressions
- `desktop/` — the Electron app (`src/` main process, `src/backend/` native backend, `setup/` status window, `bootstrap/` first-run SQL); `scripts/desktop/` builds, packages and smoke-tests it; `.github/workflows/desktop.yml` runs that and drafts releases
- `docs/` — the GitHub Pages landing page (https://indkhan.github.io/Moneo/); its download button reads the latest published release

Imports go one way: `app/` → `components/` → `lib/` and `workflows/`. `lib/finance/` never imports `lib/ai/`, and Electron stays in `desktop/src`. Lint enforces all of it (`moneo/import-boundaries`); code that two layers need lives in the lower one.

## Rules and what enforces them

## Sign-in callbacks and addresses

Each outside service sends the browser back to a different address. Keep these in mind before changing ports, hosts or remote access:

- **Sign in with ChatGPT** (`lib/ai/chatgpt.ts`): OpenAI only accepts the loopback `http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/api/ai/chatgpt/callback`, so sign-in happens on the computer running Moneo. Tokens are stored there, so chat works from any device afterwards.
- **Enable Banking** (`lib/bank/return-listener.ts`): production apps need an `https://` redirect registered in the Enable Banking app. Moneo uses `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback` (a local listener with a cert from `npm run setup`), which forwards to `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`.
- **Scalable Capital** (`lib/scalable/server.ts`): dynamic client registration with `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL/api/scalable/callback`. `localhost` registers freely; other hosts need Scalable's allowlist (it rejects `*.ts.net`).
- **Supabase** (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `127.0.0.1:54321`): only the server may call it; never send the browser there, or it breaks on other devices.
- **Desktop app**: the same callbacks on the app's own port (47300 by default) instead of 3000.
- **Phone and tablet** (`*.ts.net` through Tailscale Serve): the laptop's addresses above never change. The three logins refuse to start from a remote device (`lib/remote-device.ts`) and say to use the computer; everything else, including sync, works from there.
- **Voice** needs a secure context (https or localhost) for the microphone.

## Database changes

Add a new ordered migration in `supabase/migrations/`, keep `lib/schema.ts` aligned and run `npm run db:types`. Never rewrite an applied migration. `npm run setup` applies pending ones and records them in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. For other Supabase CLI commands use `npx supabase ... --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL"` (from `.env`).

## Tests

A test earns its place by failing when real behaviour breaks. Before writing one, name the bug it would catch.

- **Write tests for** money math, imports and undo, auth, RLS and AI scopes, concurrency, and bugs that actually happened (name the PR or issue).
- **Don't write tests that** assert UI copy or labels, grep source or migration files, mirror the implementation, or need more than about three `vi.mock`s to run. Test the `lib/` function instead.
- Check each test against two imagined edits. Break the behaviour (a wrong value, a skipped or doubled effect): the test must fail. Restructure the internals without changing any result: the test must still pass. Rewrite or delete a test that misses either. Take the expected value from the requirement, never from a run of the code, and never assert on data the test built itself.
- One test per behaviour. Don't add a test per requirement or per audit finding; if an existing test covers the failure, extend it.
- `npm test` must pass with no `.env`, no Docker and no network. Anything that needs the database is a `*.live.test.ts`.
- Use fake timers or controlled promises, never real waits. Mock AI, bank and Scalable; real calls are opt-in only.
- Test files share one loaded app (`isolate: false`) and run in random order. `vitest.setup.ts` puts back timers, env, globals, spies, loaded modules and `process.env` after each file; anything else a test changes (a fixture object, a file, a module's own state) it resets in `beforeEach`. A test never relies on what an earlier test left behind. For a module that keeps state, take a fresh copy per test with `vi.resetModules()` and `await import()`. A failure seen only in some orders is such a leak: rerun with the printed seed (`--sequence.seed=<n>`) and fix it.
- Browser specs are for whole user journeys, not single links or labels. Add a spec only when no existing journey can take the check.
- When you remove a feature, remove its tests. Never delete or skip a failing test just to get green: fix the cause, or ask.
- If a pointless test lands, find out why the agent wrote it and fix the guidance here.

Run the smallest relevant test while iterating. Before finishing, run `npm test`, `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck`; add `npm run build` for app, config or build changes, and Playwright for changed user flows. CI runs the same checks on every pull request, and `npm run test:db` against a fresh test backend.

## Commits and pull requests

- Break the work into steps and commit each one; a big task is several commits.
- Write commit messages in plain language: what changed and why.
- Deferred work gets their issue created on github.
- Stacked PRs: before merging a PR that another open PR is based on, change the dependent PR's base to `main`; deleting the merged branch otherwise closes it.
- Every PR that changes code has a **Speed** section: how long the app takes to open and how long the changed action takes, before and after (skill `measure-speed`). If something got slower, the change caused it: fix it before opening the PR, or say why it cannot be faster and ask. Docs-only PRs write "No runtime change".
- A PR that changes what the owner sees embeds its screenshots and recordings in the description (skill `verify-ui`). A path to a local folder is not enough.
- Long agent prompts and plans don't get committed; if guidance must persist, put the rule in AGENTS.md.
- suggest edits in agents.md if there was something that is changed or needs to be there in agents.md but only suggest when it is actually needed dont suggest just for suggesting.(only for prs)

## Context

Read only what the task needs: `.env.example` for environment names, `e2e/README.md` for browser tests, `supabase/tests/README.md` for SQL checks.

# AGENTS.md

Moneo is an open-source personal-finance app you run on your own computer. One owner imports statements or syncs a bank, tracks accounts and wealth, plans spending, and asks about their money in chat, artifacts and voice calls.

Moneo ships two ways from this one codebase: the desktop app (`desktop/`, Electron, what most owners install) and the source installation (`npm run setup` + Docker). Every change must work in both.

Stack: Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript. The backend is Postgres plus the open-source Supabase Auth, PostgREST and Storage services: in Docker for the source installation (`docker-compose.yml`), as bundled native processes in the desktop app (`desktop/src/backend/`). Drizzle schema, Workflow (local world) for durable jobs, Vitest and Playwright, and the Vercel AI SDK, paid by the owner's ChatGPT plan or an API key.

These are defaults. The developer's instructions override them; if a rule conflicts with the task, say so and ask.

## Non-negotiables

- **Local-first.** Everything listens on `127.0.0.1`; optional phone access is Tailscale forwarding to it (`lib/phone-access.ts`). Data leaves the machine only for services the owner set up (AI provider, Enable Banking, Scalable). New features must work fully offline from the cloud except those calls.
- **One owner, no accounts.** The proxy signs the owner in automatically; there is no sign-up or sign-in screen. Private access from the owner's own Tailscale devices needs no login; anything public must add one first.
- **Financial truth comes from code and data, never from AI guesses.** Money is integer minor units (`bigint`) with an explicit currency. The AI explains and proposes; every write it suggests is a card the owner accepts.
- **Two AI writes skip cards.** The organizer applies high- and medium-confidence category and merchant labels itself, marked as AI (`organized_by = 'ai'`), listed with every other AI decision and undoable; they never become owner rules or owner corrections. The chat tool `transactions_setCategory` sets the category the owner named for the exact transaction they named, audited and undoable. Every other AI write is a card.
- **History is kept.** Preserve source records, corrections, history and undo when changing financial data flows.
- **Open source.** No secrets, private statements or personal data in the repo (`npm run check:privacy` runs before tests and lint).

## How to work

1. **Think before coding.** State your assumptions. If a request has more than one reading, name them and ask instead of picking silently. If a simpler approach exists, say so.
2. **Simplicity first.** Write the least code that solves the problem: no speculative features, options or single-use abstractions. Prefer existing utilities and dependencies, and Zod for validating user and external input. Would a senior engineer call it overcomplicated? Then simplify.
3. **Surgical changes.** Touch only what the task needs and match the nearby style. Remove what your own change made unused; mention unrelated dead code instead of deleting it.
4. **Never write a comment.** Put the meaning in a name, a type, a test or a lint rule; if a comment would defend a workaround, fix the cause instead. `npm run lint` rejects comments (`moneo/no-comments` in `eslint.config.mjs`) except tool directives such as `eslint-disable-next-line <rule> -- reason`.
5. **Corrections become checks.** When a review correction could recur, enforce it with a lint rule, a type or a test whose error message says what to do instead. Add a line here only when it needs human judgment.
6. **Fix the class, not the case.** Trace a failure to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there, so every similar case is fixed with it. A guard, a retry, a swallowed error or a special case at the place it showed up hides the fault. When the assistant in the app cannot do something, give it the tool, data or scope it lacks; never add a sentence to its system prompt (`lib/ai/provider.ts`, `lib/ai/voice-*`) that names one request, keyword or example.
7. **Goal-driven.** Turn the task into checks you can run, then loop until they pass. A bug fix starts by reproducing the failure; see Tests for when that becomes a kept test. Purely visual changes get before/after screenshots instead (skill `verify-ui`).

## Safety

- Never run tests or experiments against the owner's backend (`.env`, Docker project `moneo`, app on port 3000). Tests use the separate test backend below, as its QA user or disposable users they create and remove.
- Never delete the `moneo` Docker volumes (`docker compose down -v`) or drop its database: that is the owner's financial history. The test backend is disposable: `docker compose -p moneo-qa down -v` then `npm run setup -- --qa` starts it fresh.
- Never change `JWT_SECRET`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` or `BANK_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in an existing `.env`; keys, sessions and stored bank and ChatGPT tokens stop working.
- Never commit `.env*` (except `.env.example`), `.data/`, `e2e/.auth.json` or `.qa/`.
- Only kill processes you started, or ones you verified by port and working directory. Never kill by name.
- Real AI, bank and Scalable calls cost money or count against limits (PSD2 allows about 4 background bank fetches a day). Mock them in tests unless the task is to check the real service.

## Hit every surface

Before calling a feature done, check where else it shows up:

- `FEATURES.md` (generated by `npm run feature-map`) lists every page, chat tool, voice route, widget, palette command, background job and undo path; find the feature's other entry points there.
- Pages and their mobile layout, light and dark.
- Chat tools and the system prompt in `lib/ai/provider.ts`, artifacts, and the voice call (`lib/ai/voice-*`).
- Home widgets and the command palette.
- Background jobs (`lib/scheduler.ts`, `workflows/`) and imports from files, banks and Scalable.
- The desktop app: see Desktop app below.
- The reverse path: undo, reset all data, reconnect, disconnect.
- Docs: `README.md` for anything the owner sets up or runs, the landing page in `docs/` when a headline feature or install step changes, `.env.example` for new variables. Deferred work goes in GitHub issues.

- Feature map: `npm run feature-map` regenerates `FEATURES.md`

- Database: `npm run test:db` (needs the backend from `npm run setup`) · `npm run db:types` regenerates `lib/database.types.ts` after a migration (needs the test backend)
- E2E: `npm run test:e2e` (see `e2e/README.md`)
- Desktop: `node scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs --platform <win-x64|mac-arm64|mac-x64|linux-x64>` once, then `npm run desktop:build`, `npm run desktop:dev`, `npm run desktop:dist` and `npm run desktop:smoke` (drives the packaged app)

Everything that needs a database or a running app is tested against `moneo-qa`, never the owner's setup:

- **Reset:** `npm run qa:reset` empties the QA workspace. Each spec should still set up the state it needs rather than rely on what earlier runs left behind.
- `npm run test:db` and the `supabase/tests/*.mjs` scripts read `.env.qa` only.
- A nightly run (`npm run qa:nightly`, see `e2e/README.md`) runs every spec twice and keeps the issue "Nightly browser suite is failing" up to date; fix what it lists before adding new specs.

## Desktop app

The Electron app (`desktop/README.md`, `desktop/src/backend/README.md`) runs the same Next.js server as a standalone build next to its own Postgres, GoTrue, PostgREST and Storage processes. There is no Docker, Node.js, terminal or `.env` on the owner's machine, so:

- **Migrations run on the owner's existing database** at the next start, after an automatic `pre-upgrade` backup (`desktop/src/backend/migrations.ts`). They must work without the extensions the bundle lacks: supautils, pg_graphql, pg_net, pg_cron, pgsodium/vault, pg_stat_statements, realtime, and uuid-ossp on Windows.
- **The app lives on `http://localhost:47300`** (or the port saved in `shell.json`), not 3000. Get addresses from the request or from `appUrl()`, `loopbackUrl()` and `appPort()` in `lib/env.ts`; lint rejects a hard-coded 3000.
- **Sign-ins open in the system browser** and return through the loopback callbacks; the result reaches the window through `lib/desktop-bridge.ts` and `desktop/src/bridge.ts`. The window opens only Moneo's own pages and allows only the microphone and copying.
- **Files the server reads at runtime** by a dynamic path need `/*turbopackIgnore: true*/`, or the standalone build traces source files and `desktop:build` fails.
- **A new backend service, native module or data folder** must be added to `fetch-backend.mjs`, the start order, backup and restore, and the packaged files in `electron-builder.config.cjs`.
- **Keep the security fuses** (RunAsNode, `NODE_OPTIONS` and `--inspect` off; asar integrity on); `desktop:smoke` reads them back.
- Never test against the owner's installed app or its user-data folder; set `MONEO_DESKTOP_HOME` to a scratch folder.

## Sign-in callbacks and addresses

Each outside service sends the browser back to a different address. Keep these in mind before changing ports, hosts or remote access:

- **Sign in with ChatGPT** (`lib/ai/chatgpt.ts`): OpenAI only accepts the loopback `http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/api/ai/chatgpt/callback`, so sign-in happens on the computer running Moneo. Tokens are stored there, so chat works from any device afterwards.
- **Enable Banking** (`lib/bank/return-listener.ts`): production apps need an `https://` redirect registered in the Enable Banking app. Moneo uses `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback` (a local listener with a cert from `npm run setup`), which forwards to `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`.
- **Scalable Capital** (`lib/scalable/server.ts`): dynamic client registration with `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL/api/scalable/callback`. `localhost` registers freely; other hosts need Scalable's allowlist (it rejects `*.ts.net`).
- **Supabase** (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `127.0.0.1:54321`): only the server may call it; never send the browser there, or it breaks on other devices.
- **Desktop app**: the same callbacks on the app's own port (47300 by default) instead of 3000.
- **Phone and tablet** (`*.ts.net` through Tailscale Serve): the laptop's addresses above never change. The three logins refuse to start from a remote device (`lib/remote-device.ts`) and say to use the computer; everything else, including sync, works from there.
- **Voice** needs a secure context (https or localhost) for the microphone.

Add a new ordered migration in `supabase/migrations/`, keep `lib/schema.ts` aligned and run `npm run db:types`. Never rewrite an applied migration. `npm run setup` applies pending ones and records them in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. For other Supabase CLI commands use `npx supabase ... --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL"` (from `.env`).

## Tests

A test earns its place by failing when real behaviour breaks. Before writing one, name the bug it would catch.

- **Write tests for** money math, imports and undo, auth, RLS and AI scopes, concurrency, and bugs that actually happened (name the PR or issue).
- **Don't write tests that** assert UI copy or labels, grep source or migration files, mirror the implementation, or need more than about three `vi.mock`s to run. Test the `lib/` function instead.
- Check each test against two imagined edits. Break the behaviour (a wrong value, a skipped or doubled effect): the test must fail. Restructure the internals without changing any result: the test must still pass. Rewrite or delete a test that misses either. Take the expected value from the requirement, never from a run of the code, and never assert on data the test built itself.
- One test per behaviour. Don't add a test per requirement or per audit finding; if an existing test covers the failure, extend it.
- `npm test` must pass with no `.env`, no Docker and no network. Anything that needs the database is a `*.live.test.ts`.
- Use fake timers or controlled promises, never real waits. Mock AI, bank and Scalable; real calls are opt-in only.
- Test files share one loaded app (`isolate: false`) and run in random order. `vitest.setup.ts` puts back timers, env, globals, spies, loaded modules and `process.env` after each file; anything else a test changes (a fixture object, a file, a module's own state) it resets in `beforeEach`. A test never relies on what an earlier test left behind. For a module that keeps state, take a fresh copy per test with `vi.resetModules()` and `await import()`. A failure seen only in some orders is such a leak: rerun with the printed seed (`--sequence.seed=<n>`) and fix it.
- Browser specs are for whole user journeys, not single links or labels. Add a spec only when no existing journey can take the check.
- When you remove a feature, remove its tests. Never delete or skip a failing test just to get green: fix the cause, or ask.
- If a pointless test lands, find out why the agent wrote it and fix the guidance here.

Run the smallest relevant test while iterating. Before finishing, run `npm test`, `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck`; add `npm run build` for app, config or build changes, and Playwright for changed user flows. tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types. This does not cover the `web-fetch` agent type where it is listed and you have no WebFetch tool of your own: it stands in for that tool, so calling it to read a page is ordinary tool use.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort.
